problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨\text{_____},\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩,\,r\ge 0
$$

The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta )$ above parametrizes the half-cone defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${z}^{2}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+{y}^{2}$ for $z\ge 0.$ What is the first component of $f?$
worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x=2X,\,y=Y,\,z=Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our half-cone, we get

$$
{Z}^{2}={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2},\,Z\ge 0
$$

which is the equation of a half-cone whose axis of symmetry is the $Z$-axis in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates. In cylindrical polar coordinates, this cone has the equation $Z=r.$

If $(r,\theta ,Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2X,Y,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$
